scope: Named actors, institutions, material states and evidential limits in the 1831-1833 British trial of Nepali paper material.

primary_event.material: Nipal/Nepal paper stuff dried and formed into transport bricks
primary_event.origin_chain: Himalayan/Nepal paper-material network -> Calcutta/Bengal government forwarding -> Edinburgh scientific relay -> Scottish papermaker trial
primary_event.published_report: Journal of the Asiatic Society of Bengal 2 (1833), Asiatic Society Proceedings, p.93
primary_event.result: British remanufacture failed to reproduce the softness and toughness of finished Nepal-made sheets.

actors.name: George Swinton
actors.role: Chief Secretary to the Government of Bengal; material/specimen forwarder and administrative-commercial broker
secure_evidence: JASB says dried pulp was sent home by G. Swinton in 1831
BL India Office catalogue identifies Swinton as Chief Secretary and documents parallel trans-imperial material-testing operations

actors.name: John Robison
actors.role: General Secretary, Royal Society of Edinburgh; scientific-society broker
secure_evidence: JASB calls him Sec. Ed. Roy. Society
contemporary records identify John Robison as RSE General Secretary 1828-1840

actors.name: Charles Cowan
actors.role: professional Scottish papermaker; worked up Nepal pulp and supplied specimens/notes/valuation
secure_evidence: JASB first says Mr C. Cowan, then explicitly names Mr Charles Cowan and calls him the manufacturer
Charles Cowan was a professional papermaker associated with the Cowan Penicuik/Valleyfield enterprise
industrial_context: Cowan family operated several Penicuik-area paper mills
not_yet_secure: exact mill where Nepal trial was performed
specific apparatus/process used for the trial

institutions.name: Government of Bengal / Calcutta
institutions.role: sample transmission, administrative and commercial evaluation node

institutions.name: Scottish papermaking industry / Cowan enterprise
institutions.role: technical working-up, specimen production, grade/value assessment

institutions.name: Asiatic Society of Bengal
institutions.role: publication and recirculation of technical result in India

comparative_control.material: thin finished sheets made in Nepal and sent to Britain in 1829
reported_properties: took minute bank-note plate impression with perfect fidelity
comparative_control.significance: Finished sheets preserved high-performance properties that British remanufacture from dried pulp failed to reproduce.

commercial_assessment: nearly double if fit for cartridge paper
no hopes for more refined use after trial
Cowan_trial_properties.exact_figures_warning: Bleaching reagent quantities in searchable OCR should be image-verified before publication quotation.

Swinton_comparative_program.procedure: Calcutta experiment/material -> Government note -> Court of Directors/England -> specialist market testing
Swinton_comparative_program.interpretation: The Nepal paper trial belongs to a broader administrative technique of trans-imperial material sampling and commercial/scientific evaluation.

research_priority: Search Royal Society of Edinburgh incoming correspondence to John Robison 1831-33 for Swinton/Cowan/Nipal paper material
Search Alexander Cowan & Sons / Valleyfield business archive and Charles Cowan papers for Nepal/Nipal paper trial notes
Locate trial sheets and strongly bleached specimen if surviving
Determine exact sheet-formation method of Cowan trial
